DataSourceSetupGuide({'steps': [{'label': 'Create a Sentry User Auth Token', 'detail': 'Generate a token in Sentry with read scopes so Holmes can query issues and projects.', 'kind': 'app_config', 'instructions': '- Sign in to Sentry and open **User Settings → Auth Tokens**
  - https://sentry.io/settings/account/api/auth-tokens/
- Click **Create New Token**
- Grant at minimum these read scopes: `org:read`, `project:read`, `event:read`, `member:read`
- Copy the token value - you will paste it into a Kubernetes secret in the next step
- Note your Sentry **organization slug** (visible in the URL, e.g. `https://sentry.io/organizations/<org-slug>/`) - you can pass it to Holmes at query time', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Create the Kubernetes secret', 'detail': 'Store the Sentry token in the robusta namespace so the runner can read it.', 'kind': 'secret', 'instructions': '', 'command': "kubectl create secret generic sentry-mcp-token -n robusta --from-literal=token='<your-sentry-user-auth-token>'", 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Add the Sentry MCP server to your Helm values', 'detail': 'Merge this snippet into your existing generated_values.yaml.', 'kind': 'helm', 'instructions': '', 'command': '', 'yaml': 'holmes:
  additionalEnvVars:
    - name: SENTRY_MCP_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: sentry-mcp-token
          key: token
  mcp_servers:
    sentry-custom:
      description: "Sentry MCP - read issues, errors, and projects from Sentry."
      icon_url: "https://sentry.io/_static/f39a5674f65e46a666f5b32c81a3f0f2/logos/favicon.ico"
      docs_url: "https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/"
      config:
        url: "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"
        mode: streamable-http
        headers:
          Authorization: "Bearer <env.SENTRY_MCP_TOKEN>"
      llm_instructions: |
        ## When to use Sentry

        Use this data source whenever the user asks about **application errors, exceptions, crashes, releases, or Sentry projects**, or when investigating why a service is throwing errors in production.

        ## What to do

        - To answer **"what's in Sentry?"** or **"which projects exist?"** - call the Sentry `projects` / `list projects` tool first (scoped to the user's organization slug).
        - To investigate **errors / exceptions / crashes** - call the Sentry `issues` tool (list/search issues) and then fetch the details of the most relevant issue (including stacktrace, event count, and last-seen timestamp).
        - Always ask the user for the Sentry **organization slug** if it's not obvious from context, and pass it to the tools.
        - Prefer **read-only** Sentry operations. Do **not** resolve, ignore, delete, or otherwise mutate Sentry issues - this data source is configured for diagnostics only.
        - When correlating with Kubernetes: match the Sentry `environment` / `release` / service name to the workload the user is asking about.'}, {'label': 'Apply the Helm upgrade', 'detail': 'Deploy the new values to the alon-elish-cluster runner.', 'kind': 'deploy', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'helm upgrade robusta robusta/robusta --values=generated_values.yaml --set clusterName=alon-elish-cluster', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Verify the connection', 'detail': 'Confirm Holmes has picked up Sentry after the restart.', 'kind': 'verify', 'instructions': '- Wait for the Helm upgrade to finish and the Holmes pod in the `robusta` namespace to restart and become `Ready`
- Open the **Data Sources** page in Robusta and confirm **Sentry** (key `sentry-custom`) is listed as connected
- Ask Holmes something like **"List my Sentry projects for org `<your-org-slug>`"** or **"Show the top open Sentry issues for `<project>`"** and confirm it returns real data', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}]})

DataSourceSetupGuide({'steps': [{'label': 'Create a Sentry User Auth Token', 'detail': 'Generate a personal API token in Sentry with read scopes for issues and projects.', 'kind': 'app_config', 'instructions': '- Sign in to Sentry and open User Settings
- Go to **Auth Tokens** and click **Create New Token**
  - https://sentry.io/settings/account/api/auth-tokens/
- Grant at minimum these read scopes:
  - `org:read`
  - `project:read`
  - `event:read`
  - `member:read`
- Copy the token value (starts with `sntryu_`) - you will paste it into the Kubernetes secret in the next step', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Create the Kubernetes secret', 'detail': 'Stores your Sentry auth token so Holmes can read it at runtime.', 'kind': 'secret', 'instructions': '', 'command': "kubectl create secret generic sentry-mcp-token -n robusta --from-literal=token='<paste-your-sentry-auth-token>'", 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Merge these values into your generated_values.yaml', 'detail': 'Adds the vendor-hosted Sentry MCP server under holmes.mcp_servers.', 'kind': 'helm', 'instructions': '', 'command': '', 'yaml': 'holmes:
  additionalEnvVars:
    - name: SENTRY_MCP_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: sentry-mcp-token
          key: token
  mcp_servers:
    sentry-custom:
      description: "Sentry hosted MCP server - read Sentry issues, errors, and projects"
      icon_url: "https://sentry.io/_assets/logos/sentry-glyph-black.svg"
      docs_url: "https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/"
      config:
        url: "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"
        mode: streamable-http
        headers:
          Authorization: "Bearer <env.SENTRY_MCP_TOKEN>"
      llm_instructions: |
        ## When to use this data source
        Use the **Sentry** MCP server whenever an investigation involves application errors, exceptions, or crash reports that a service may have reported to Sentry - especially when correlating a Kubernetes issue (crash loop, 5xx spike, deploy) with recent application-level errors.

        ## What to do
        - **List projects** with `find_projects` when the user asks what is monitored or you need a project slug/ID for other calls.
        - **Find and read issues/errors** with `find_issues` (search by project, query, status, or time range) and then `get_issue_details` for a specific issue to read the exception, stack trace, tags, and latest events.
        - Prefer scoping queries by `project` and a recent time window over broad org-wide searches.

        ## Constraints
        - **Read-only.** Do NOT resolve, ignore, assign, comment on, or otherwise mutate Sentry issues - only fetch and summarize.
        - If a required `organization_slug` or `project_slug` is unknown, list projects first instead of guessing.'}, {'label': 'Apply the Helm upgrade', 'detail': 'Rolls out the new configuration to the Robusta runner on alon-elish-cluster.', 'kind': 'deploy', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'helm upgrade robusta robusta/robusta --values=generated_values.yaml --set clusterName=alon-elish-cluster', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Verify the connection', 'detail': 'Confirm Holmes picked up the new MCP server after it restarts.', 'kind': 'verify', 'instructions': '- Wait for the Helm upgrade to finish and the Holmes pod in the `robusta` namespace to become Ready
- Open the Data Sources list in Robusta and confirm **sentry-custom** appears and is healthy
- Ask Holmes: *"List my Sentry projects"* or *"Show recent Sentry issues for project <slug>"* and verify it returns results', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}]})

DataSourceSetupGuide({'steps': [{'label': 'Create a Sentry User Auth Token', 'detail': 'Generate a token with read scopes for issues, events, and projects.', 'kind': 'app_config', 'instructions': "- Go to Sentry: **Settings → Account → API → Auth Tokens** (or open https://sentry.io/settings/account/api/auth-tokens/ )
- Click **Create New Token**
- Give it a name like `holmes-mcp`
- Grant these read scopes (sufficient for reading issues/errors and listing projects):
  - `org:read`
  - `project:read`
  - `event:read`
  - `team:read`
- Copy the token value now (you can't view it again later)
- If you're on self-hosted Sentry instead of sentry.io, note the hostname — you'll want the stdio flow rather than the hosted endpoint used below

Ref: https://mcp.sentry.dev and https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-mcp", 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Create the Kubernetes secret', 'detail': 'Store the Sentry auth token in the `robusta` namespace so the Holmes pod can read it.', 'kind': 'secret', 'instructions': '', 'command': "kubectl create secret generic sentry-mcp-token -n robusta --from-literal=token='<paste-your-sentry-auth-token-here>'", 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Add the Helm values', 'detail': 'Merge this snippet into your existing generated_values.yaml under `holmes:`.', 'kind': 'helm', 'instructions': '', 'command': '', 'yaml': 'holmes:
  additionalEnvVars:
    - name: SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: sentry-mcp-token
          key: token
  mcp_servers:
    sentry-custom:
      description: "Sentry remote MCP server - read issues, errors, and projects."
      docs_url: "https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/"
      config:
        url: "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"
        mode: streamable-http
        headers:
          Authorization: "Sentry-Bearer <env.SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN>"
      llm_instructions: |
        ## When to use this data source
        Use the **Sentry** MCP tools whenever the user is investigating application errors, crashes, exceptions, unhandled promise rejections, regressions, or performance issues surfaced by Sentry, or when they ask what projects / environments exist in Sentry.

        ## What to do
        - To answer *"what Sentry projects do we have?"* or to scope other queries, list organizations and projects first (e.g. `find_organizations`, `find_projects`).
        - To investigate an error / exception / crash the user mentioned, look up the corresponding **issue** in Sentry (e.g. `find_issues`, `get_issue_details`, `get_issue_summary`) and read its recent `events` to get the stack trace, breadcrumbs, tags, and environment.
        - When the user gives you a Sentry issue ID, short ID, or a Sentry URL, resolve it directly with the get-issue tool instead of searching.
        - Prefer **read-only / diagnostic** tools. Do NOT assign, resolve, comment on, or otherwise mutate Sentry issues.

        ## Constraints
        - You need an **organization slug** and usually a **project slug** to scope most queries; ask the user or infer from context if unclear.
        - Include the stack trace and top tags in your answer when reporting on a Sentry issue.'}, {'label': 'Apply the Helm upgrade', 'detail': 'Roll out the new configuration to the Robusta release.', 'kind': 'deploy', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'helm upgrade robusta robusta/robusta --values=generated_values.yaml --set clusterName=alon-elish-cluster', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Verify the connection', 'detail': 'Confirm Holmes picked up the new MCP server and can call it.', 'kind': 'verify', 'instructions': '- Wait for the Helm upgrade to finish and the Holmes pod to restart
- Open the Robusta UI → **Data Sources** and confirm `sentry-custom` is listed as connected
- Ask Holmes something that exercises Sentry, e.g. *"List my Sentry projects"* or *"Show me the latest Sentry issues for project <slug>"*
- If the call fails with 401/403, re-check the token scopes and that the secret contains the raw token (no `Bearer ` prefix, no quotes)', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}]})
